title.en: Bit-vector SMT: model, wraparound and proof boundary

summary: Keep width, modular arithmetic, signed interpretation and solver evidence explicit.
objective: Build a finite bit-vector SMT inspector where I set widths and signedness, check a returned SAT model, and distinguish solver-reported UNSAT from an independently checked proof.
intent_signals: distinguish UNSAT result from checked proof
example_prompts: Show why an 8-bit x can satisfy x+1=0, then compare unsigned x<1 with signed x<1 and expose the solver evidence boundary.
negative_signals: Not integer arithmetic, floating-point theory, symbolic-width reasoning, hardware equivalence for arbitrary circuits or a universal proof-certificate checker.
not_for: No symbolic or zero widths, quantifiers, arrays, floating point, optimizer, automatic solver installation or unsupported proof-format verification.

entities.name: Word lanes
entities.guidance: Blender supplies a reusable bit-cell rail, carry arc and result card. Three.js instantiates exactly m cells, labels MSB/LSB and renders the same bits under unsigned and two-complement signed interpretations.

entities.name: Evidence panel
entities.guidance: Keep formula hash, backend/version, result, model values, model re-evaluation and proof availability as separate fields; never badge a solver response as a checked proof merely because its animation completed.

state_contract.model: Quantifier-free formulas over k variables of fixed positive widths m_i, with a bounded supported operator set: equality, Boolean connectives, bvnot, bvand, bvor, bvadd, extract, concat and explicit signed/unsigned comparisons. Bit-vector values are exact bit strings; arithmetic results reduce modulo 2^m. Track not-run/running/sat/unsat/unknown/error separately. Bind results to the exact formula, declarations and backend version. On SAT, store a complete model for declared variables and re-evaluate every supported assertion. On UNSAT, label only solver-reported UNSAT unless an emitted proof artifact is accepted by a named independent checker; proof-unavailable and proof-unchecked remain visible. For tiny presets, exhaustive enumeration visits product_i 2^(m_i) assignments and may independently establish SAT/UNSAT when completed.
state_contract.authority: The exact formula and evidence object own status. Blender creates stable word-lane geometry; Three.js owns parsing, exact bit operations, backend calls/imports, enumeration and reset.
actions: Edit widths, signed/unsigned operators or assertions and invalidate all previous results.
Check using an available backend, import provenance-labeled output, or exhaustively enumerate a tiny preset.
Inspect a SAT model bit by bit and replay exact assertion evaluation.
Request proof display only when a proof artifact exists; otherwise preserve the solver-result boundary.

invariants: Operands to fixed-width binary operators have the declared compatible widths; reject width-zero, implicit widening and ambiguous signedness.
For width m, bvadd is reduced modulo 2^m; in 8 bits #xFF + #x01 = #x00.
The same bit pattern can have different signed and unsigned integer interpretations; labels and comparison operators must declare which one is used.
A SAT badge requires a model that re-evaluates all supported assertions. An unknown/error result is not UNSAT, and solver-reported UNSAT is not automatically an independently checked proof.
motion_guidance: Step commits one discrete semantic action; pause freezes playback without changing committed state. Reset cancels pending animation and restores the complete preset, including clock, history, selection and error state.
Use a static before/after view and readable tables for reduced motion. Camera movement and token/message travel only explain a committed transition.
creative_affordances: Blender may shape distinctive, stable parts and materials for the chosen metaphor; Three.js binds those parts to model IDs and derives every label, highlight and transform from semantic state. Color is reinforced with text, shape or pattern.
The layout may be sculptural, planar or spatial, provided ordering, identity and invalid states remain unambiguous.
known_limits: Finite, quantifier-free supported operators only. Solver proof syntax and trust vary; unsupported nodes make local model/proof checking unavailable rather than guessed.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no Blender export, solver, allocator, TLS stack, browser, renderer or interactive artifact was run.

physical_contract.scope: Bits and solver evidence are exact symbolic state; lights, motion and contact do not perform inference.

object_craft.structure: Build modular bit-cell strips with a removable signed-interpretation bracket, explicit carry-out gutter and formula/evidence cards arranged as distinct layers.
object_craft.material: Use paired texture/pattern states for 0/1 and an outline for model-assigned cells; never use green alone to mean verified.

claims.statement: SMT-LIB fixed-size bit-vectors have positive fixed width; bv2nat ranges from 0 to 2^m-1, the signed interpretation subtracts 2^m when the top bit is set, and bvadd is defined through conversion back to width m, giving modular arithmetic.
claims.scope: SMT-LIB 2.7 FixedSizeBitVectors theory as updated 2025-09-09; supported operators declared by this recipe.

source_refs.locator: Sort and function declarations; definition of bv2nat, bv2int, nat2bv[m] and bvadd

claims.statement: The Z3 C API retrieves a model after a satisfiable check when model construction is enabled; proof retrieval requires proof generation to have been enabled and the last result to be UNSAT, while unknown is a separate result with a reason API.
claims.scope: Z3 API result and artifact availability; no claim that a returned proof was independently checked.
